clue.text: Finding money in a book is worrying

definitions.note: an adjective phrase; the answer is the adjective worrying, with is as part of the predicate

indicators.note: in tells us the currency word sits inside the word for a book

parts.note: a tome is a large book
roubles are the money of Russia

explanation.surface: Someone discovers cash tucked between the pages of a book and finds it unsettling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finding' is only a link, and the rouble is the Russian currency; 'in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something troublesome causes bother and anxiety, so it is a fair synonym for worrying.

clue.text: Fighting men getting together would be unusual

parts.note: the RA, the Royal Artillery, is a body of British soldiers
the RE, the Royal Engineers, is another British army corps

explanation.surface: Soldiers joining up together would be an odd sight.
explanation.walkthrough: One phrase, 'Fighting men', supplies two British army corps, the Royal Artillery and the Royal Engineers; 'getting together' just joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rare is seldom found or seen, which is what unusual means.

clue.text: There's nothing in German and that's not approved of

indicators.note: in tells us the word for nothing goes inside the German word

parts.note: und is the German word for and
love means nothing, a zero score in tennis

explanation.surface: A speaker says there is nothing in German and it is frowned upon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'German and' looks like a list of topics but means the German word for and; 'in' is the container signal, and love is zero in tennis scoring.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unloved is not cared for or favoured by others, close to being disapproved of.

clue.text: Strike the trainee as hard

parts.note: L stands for learner, as on a learner driver's L-plate
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: An instruction to hit the new recruit as forcefully as possible.
explanation.walkthrough: L for a learner comes from the L-plate a British learner driver must display.
explanation.definitionFit: To lash is to hit with a whip or blow, a form of striking.

clue.text: A certain politician rates on frenziedly

indicators.note: frenziedly says the letters of rates on are thrown wildly into a new order

explanation.surface: A politician goes on ranting about rates in a frenzy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frenziedly' rearranges RATES ON.
explanation.definitionFit: A senator is a member of a senate, so one particular kind of politician.

clue.text: In short, a state body

definitions.meaning: .... is the short form of Massachusetts, a US state
a body of matter or a large group

explanation.definitionFit: Massachusetts is abbreviated Mass., and a mass is also a physical body or bulk.

clue.text: Support for a wicked type of lighting

definitions.text: Support for a wicked type of lighting

parts.words: Support for a wicked type of lighting
parts.note: wicked reads as evil but means having a wick; the holder supports a light with a wick

explanation.definitionFit: A candle has a wick, and the stand that holds it upright is the support for that light.

clue.text: Stern lasses agitating for simplicity

indicators.note: agitating means stirring up, so the letters of stern lasses are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: Severe young women campaigning for a simpler way of life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'agitating' looks like the women protesting, but it rearranges STERN LASSES.
explanation.definitionFit: Artlessness is naturalness without guile or affectation, which is simplicity.

clue.text: People watching the stars — more stars on new shows

indicators.note: new says the letters of more stars on are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Observers of the sky note that more stars are showing on a new display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges MORE STARS ON; 'shows' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Astronomers are scientists who observe celestial bodies such as stars.

clue.text: Work out financial liabilities after a struggle? Delightful!

indicators.note: after says the struggle comes first and the rest follows it

parts.note: a scrum is a struggling scrimmage, as in rugby
PT, physical training, is a workout
IOUs are written promises to repay debts

explanation.surface: Sorting out one's debts after a fight would be a delight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work out' looks like a verb meaning calculate; it is a workout, physical training. 'after' says the struggle is placed first.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrumptious means delicious or very pleasing, so delightful in a looser sense.

clue.text: Inquire into place in office — one opening

parts.note: to invest someone is to install them formally in office
I is the Roman numeral one
a gate is an opening in a wall or fence

explanation.surface: Asking about a job vacancy: someone looks into installing a person in a post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opening' suggests a vacancy in the office, but it is GATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To investigate is to examine a matter systematically, to look into it.

clue.text: A direction given about quiet in the church

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical marking for quiet
SE is the compass direction south-east

explanation.surface: A churchgoer is told which way to go and asked to keep quiet inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given about' wraps SE (south-east) round P (piano), after A.
explanation.definitionFit: An apse is the domed or vaulted recess at the east end of a church, a part found within it.

clue.text: Carefully examine safety-first container

indicators.note: first, joined to safety, says take only the opening letter of that word

parts.note: a can is a metal container

explanation.surface: Inspect closely a container designed with safety as the priority.
explanation.walkthrough: 'safety-first' looks like a description of the container; it means the first letter of 'safety'.
explanation.definitionFit: To scan is to scrutinise something closely, which is examining it carefully.

clue.text: He'll scoff at the revolutionary receiving disastrous backing

indicators.note: backing says the whole assembled run is turned round to read in the other direction
receiving means one word takes the other into its middle

parts.note: red is a common term for a revolutionary or communist
dire means dreadful or disastrous

explanation.surface: A mocker jeers at a revolutionary who gets support for a calamitous plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'receiving' builds a container, and 'backing' looks like support but turns the whole assembled run round.
explanation.definitionFit: A derider is a mocker, a person who ridicules and jeers at others.

clue.text: He's plainly argumentative, though a sportsman

definitions.meaning: a row is a quarrel, so one who rows is a quarreller
one who rows a boat in a race, an oarsman

explanation.definitionFit: Read as rhyming with cow, it is someone who quarrels; rhyming with go, it is an oarsman.

clue.text: Hair-style in order?

parts.note: in order sounds like neat, but it means within a religious order of monks

explanation.definitionFit: It is the shaved crown traditionally worn by monks and friars, members of religious orders.

clue.text: General course for some post-graduate Norwegians

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A broad syllabus designed for Norwegian postgraduate students.
explanation.walkthrough: The run straddles post-graduaTE NORwegians.
explanation.definitionFit: The tenor of something is its general drift or purport, the overall course it takes.

clue.text: Making a note on old port

parts.note: D is a note of the musical scale
over can mean on top of, as on does

explanation.surface: Someone jots down a note about a historic harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making' is a link. DOVER in Kent, a Channel port since Roman times, gives the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Dover is the Kent harbour town, a Channel crossing point since Roman times, so an ancient port.

clue.text: Oriental and reflective woman

parts.note: E for east, the Orient

indicators.note: reflective suggests a mirror image, so the word and is read backwards

explanation.surface: A thoughtful woman from the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflective' looks like thoughtful, but it is a mirror signal turning the link-looking word 'and' round.
explanation.definitionFit: Edna is a woman's given name.

clue.text: See post gets properly dealt with

indicators.note: dealt with suggests the letters of post are handled and rearranged into order

explanation.surface: Someone checks that the mail is being handled correctly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'properly dealt with' rearranges POST; 'gets' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To spot something is to notice or catch sight of it.

clue.text: A theatrical setting

parts.note: a near-straight description of the scenery and furnishing of a stage

explanation.definitionFit: Decor is the scenery and furnishings, including a stage set for a play.

clue.text: Still aim for the sort of job which offers no prospects

definitions.text: the sort of job which offers no prospects

parts.note: dead means motionless or still
an end is a goal or aim

explanation.surface: Being motionless and aiming for a hopeless job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' reads as an adverb meaning yet; it is the adjective DEAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A dead-end job leads nowhere, with no promotion or future.

clue.text: A letter from America

parts.note: letter seems to be correspondence, but here it is one who lets property, in US usage

explanation.definitionFit: In the US an estate agent who sells or lets property is called by this title.

clue.text: Taking a drink, one may go head-over-heels!

definitions.meaning: a glass that holds a drink

explanation.definitionFit: A tumbler is a flat-bottomed drinking glass and also an acrobat who turns somersaults.

clue.text: Lying about a police trap

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a sting is an undercover operation to catch criminals

explanation.surface: Someone tells lies about an undercover police set-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lying' looks like telling untruths; it means reclining.
explanation.definitionFit: Resting means lying down to relax.

clue.text: Express discontent when fish is offered

explanation.surface: A diner grumbles when served a bony freshwater fish.
explanation.definitionFit: To carp is to complain pettily, and the carp is a common freshwater fish.

clue.text: Stick up for a European?

explanation.definitionFit: A pole is a long stick, and a Pole is a native of Poland in Europe.

clue.text: Soon making a cathedral official lose his head!

indicators.note: losing the head means dropping the first letter of the official

parts.note: a canon is a clergyman on a cathedral's staff

explanation.surface: Soon a cathedral clergyman will be beheaded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lose his head' removes the C from CANON.
explanation.definitionFit: Anon is an old-fashioned word for shortly or presently.

clue.text: A poet giving chase

definitions.meaning: Leigh ... was an English Romantic poet and essayist

explanation.definitionFit: Leigh Hunt was a Romantic poet and essayist, and to hunt is to pursue or give chase.

clue.text: Axed when rotten

indicators.note: rotten suggests decay, so the letters of when are spoiled into a new order

explanation.surface: Something was chopped down because it had gone rotten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rotten' rearranges WHEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Hewn means cut or chopped, as with an axe.

clue.text: Loses time in complicated ceremonies

indicators.note: complicated says the letters of loses time in are tangled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone wastes time in elaborate rituals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complicated' rearranges LOSES TIME IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Solemnities are formal rites or ceremonial occasions.

clue.text: A one-man band

parts.note: band seems musical, but here it is a hoop of metal tying a woman to her one man

explanation.definitionFit: It is a circular band of gold worn to show marriage to a single husband.
